criteria.description: Dashboard routes always settle into content or a bounded recoverable error instead of an indefinite loading spinner.
verification: Using seeded authenticated data, directly load, reload, and freshly navigate to `/`, `/releases`, and `/operations` at least 10 times each; every attempt renders the expected data.
Repeat with the backend deterministically delayed and then unavailable; an accessible skeleton appears without material layout movement and changes to an error state within 10 seconds.
Restore the backend and activate Retry; the route renders data without a full browser restart.
Run the deterministic frontend regression tests covering normal, delayed, and failed responses; they pass.

criteria.description: All scan triggers and other state-changing routes enforce authentication, ownership, request-origin protection, and scan concurrency limits.
verification: Call `POST /api/scans` and the equivalent backend scan route without a session; each returns 401 and the GitHub fake records no call.
With user B's session, request a scan or release action against user A's repository or record ID; each returns a generic 403 and creates no operation, audit mutation, or GitHub call.
With user A's valid session and origin, start a scan of A's selected repository; it succeeds and invokes the GitHub fake once.

Under the current Vercel limit of one concurrent user scan, attempt another while the first remains active; it returns 429 and does not invoke GitHub. Verify the configurable limit accepts values up to 10 and another user has an independent allowance.
Trigger a trusted scheduled scan while a user scan is active; it remains exempt from the user concurrency limit and still requires valid `CRON_SECRET` authentication.
Verify the protected-route matrix also covers repository selection, schedule changes, approval, rejection, publication, and any direct backend aliases.

criteria.description: Two independently authenticated GitHub accounts have isolated connections, repositories, workflow records, actions, and protected tokens.
verification: Sign in as two fake GitHub accounts with disjoint repository grants and select a repository for each.
For each user, repository selectors and `GET /api/scans` expose only that user's authorized repositories and scans.
Create scans, packs, operations, decisions, schedules, and audit events for both users; each dashboard and API session displays only its own records.
Attempt cross-user read, scan, approve, reject, and publish operations; all are denied and neither user's records nor GitHub calls are changed.
Confirm there are no shared team, organization, or application-role access paths.
Confirm the fake OAuth token canary appears in neither browser responses nor logs nor plaintext in the test database.

criteria.description: Every navigation destination and compatibility URL is directly loadable and refresh-safe.
verification: In an authenticated browser, directly load and refresh `/`, `/releases`, `/operations`, `/settings/github`, `/settings/schedule`, and a valid `/releases/{id}`; none returns 404.
Directly load `/github` and `/schedule`; each resolves or redirects to the corresponding settings page while preserving a usable refresh or bookmark URL.
Activate every sidebar link and confirm its destination renders the intended page.

criteria.description: Release-pack creation is idempotent per user, repository, and version while scan and audit history remains intact.
verification: Run the same deterministic scan twice for one user, repository, and version.
Confirm only one current release pack exists for that identity and the release list does not show a duplicate.
Confirm both scan attempts and their audit history remain queryable.
Repeat with another user or repository using the same version; a distinct current pack is created without affecting the first.

criteria.description: Operation and scan interfaces expose polished, accessible production information.
verification: Open Operations and confirm raw labels such as `Non Release manual` are replaced by human-readable wording and every operation displays a timestamp.
Call `GET /api/scans` without a session and receive 401; call it with a session and receive a list containing only that user's scans.
At a mobile viewport, measure sidebar, retry, scan, decision, and settings controls; every interactive target is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
Keyboard and accessibility inspection identifies the loading skeleton and error/retry state with meaningful accessible text.

criteria.description: Operator documentation accurately describes authentication, isolation, public routes, environment names, and separate Vercel projects without exposing values.
verification: README/operator docs identify health and OAuth entry/callback as public, protected UI and API behavior, one-account-per-user ownership, token protection, scan concurrency limits, and trusted scheduler authentication and exemption.
Docs retain separate `backend` FastAPI and `frontend` Next.js Vercel roots and state that `RELEASE_MANAGER_API_URL` is server-only.

Docs list all required environment-variable names, migration steps, and verification commands, and explain whether `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_OWNER`, and `GITHUB_REPO` are legacy or local compatibility variables.
Search the documentation and tracked examples; no real secret or OAuth token value is present.

criteria.description: The complete offline verification chain passes without deployment or cloud-resource creation.
verification: Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`; it exits successfully.
Run `npm --prefix frontend test`; it exits successfully.
Run `npm --prefix frontend run test:e2e`; it exits successfully using loopback services and deterministic fakes.
Run `npm --prefix frontend run build`; the production Next.js build exits successfully.
Confirm no deployment command ran and no cloud resource or deployment artifact was created.

note: The definition of done. Later phases may ONLY flip `passes`. Editing or removing a criterion is a gate failure.
